text:
Anton Lundell is hot, and our numbers say he's earned it. He has 8 points and 6 goals in his last ten games, including a hat trick against Winnipeg and two more against Detroit, and his own chances are up too, 3.9 expected goals in that stretch against a usual 2.8.

The odd part is the setting. Last Word On Sports wrote about Lundell in a bottom-six role on a struggling Panthers team, and he's playing a bit less lately, about 17 minutes a night. Yet Florida gets about 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, seven and a half points better than without him, and his line has scored about six fewer goals than its chances deserved. That's someone outplaying his deployment.

The two-time Cup winner has 7 goals and 11 points in 22 games, with his finishing matching his chances almost exactly. Evolving-Hockey had him facing 90th-percentile competition last season, with much of his value from the power play, where he has only one point this year. Watch whether Florida moves him up the lineup to chase goals. The case for it is in the numbers.
